items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption frames the joke through a familiar relationship or social role such as spouse, parent, boss, neighbor, or customer; judge only visible text, not whether the caption is good.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption uses plain, restrained, everyday conversational diction and understated social framing; do not judge whether that register suits the cartoon.

items.X_desc: Score the extent to which the caption relies on a simple, highly recognizable wordplay or pun that any competent writer would immediately associate with the visual elements (e.g., 'chrysalis' for 'crisis'). Do not judge if the pun is funny.
items.Y_desc: Score the extent to which the caption heavily features simple homophones, double-meanings, or direct literalizations that explicitly rely on the concrete objects in the drawing (e.g., animal sounds, food puns). Do not judge if the pun is funny.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption uses generationally or historically marked idioms, cultural references, brands, or institutional terms; judge only visible text, not whether the caption is good.
items.Y_desc: Score 0–10 for how much the caption uses time-bound news, politics, public figures, or live events; do not judge whether this makes the caption good.

items.X_desc: Score the extent to which the caption focuses on describing the literal absurdity of the drawing itself or pointing out the characters' mundane reaction to it (e.g., 'this is so much easier'). Do not judge if it is a good observation.
items.Y_desc: Score the extent to which the caption introduces a politically divisive, legally controversial, or culturally polarized real-world subject that is entirely absent from the drawing itself. Do not judge the appropriateness or humor of the subject.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption uses the most immediately suggested pun, idiom, or literal reinterpretation of a conspicuous visual element, with little individualized framing; judge only visible text, not whether the caption is good.
items.Y_desc: Score the extent to which the caption is extremely short, abandoning any narrative setup to deliver a quick, blunt conversational response (e.g., 'chicken or rabbit'). Do not judge if brevity makes it a good caption.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption is an unusually economical one-liner or fragment with immediate delivery and no explanatory scaffolding; judge only visible text, not whether the caption is good.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption uses the most immediate pun, idiom, or stock association suggested by the visible objects; do not judge whether the resulting joke is good.

anchors.X_name: Presence of a trailing apology or disclaimer
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how fully the text ends with an apology, a disclaimer, an edit note or a plea to the reader. Extent only.
anchors.Y_name: Closing self-deprecating note to the reader
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the writer signs off by apologising for the joke or hedging about it. Extent only; do not judge quality.

anchors.X_name: How much capitalised shouting the text contains
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the density of all-caps words and repeated exclamation marks. Count only; do not judge whether it is effective.
anchors.Y_name: How far the ending reinterprets the setup
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the final move makes the reader re-read the setup with a second meaning. Judge the mechanism, not the typography.
